source.title: Tune the Baseline First: Most of Muon's Scaled Weight Decay Gain Is a Tuning Gap, but Its Small Real Advantage Grows With Model Size

record.tranche_reason: The study compares held-out performance after tuning a weight-decay modification and its baseline across model sizes, using a different optimizer comparison and metric from the listed versions. It does not test any version as specifically stated.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out BPB comparisons for constant weight decay and Muon-SW, including untuned and tuned gaps, scale, schedule, and transfer-regret results. These are relevant to optimizer and explicit-regularization effects, but do not measure train-test gaps or the specific settings named by V1–V8. Cited results from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study compares two weight-decay schedules within the same Muon/AdamW recipe. It does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD, so its tuning results do not test V4. Its own results test none of V1–V8; the record's T2 classification is incorrect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. About 90% of the small-scale advantage disappears with comparable tuning, a small residual favors Muon-SW across four paired L3 seeds, and the one-dimensional tuned advantage increases across the tested ladder. The scale trend remains provisional because L4 and L6 use one seed and fitted optima outside the sampled range.
record.recipe_differences: Compares Muon-SW with constant decoupled weight decay using Muon for non-embedding 2D parameters and AdamW for other parameters; trains source-scaled MoE language models and evaluates held-out BPB. It does not use the methods or error-gap measures in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured method gap depends on whether the LR·WD product is untuned or tuned, model rung, and schedule (cosine versus WSD). L4 and L6 use one seed per setting; optimum estimates at larger rungs reach or exceed sweep edges.

fits_no_version.finding: At L3, tuning reduces the shared-setting advantage of 0.03499 BPB to 0.00261 BPB in the full two-dimensional analysis; all four paired seeds favor Muon-SW.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Comparable tuning of constant and scaled weight decay can remove most of an apparent held-out performance advantage while leaving a small residual.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the three rungs, the one-dimensional tuned difference rises from 0.00359 to 0.00514 BPB while the untuned difference decreases. Larger-rung estimates use one seed and extrapolated optima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The residual advantage of scaled weight decay after tuning can vary with model scale.

fits_no_version.finding: The optimal-product ratio is 1.41 under cosine and 0.29 under WSD; WSD is inconsistent with all three proposed ratio predictions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate schedules can change the relative optimal decay products of constant and scaled weight decay.

fits_no_version.finding: Extrapolated L6 decay products incur reported regrets of 0.00140 and 0.00202 BPB.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transferring decay-product optima across scales can incur held-out performance regret.

record.problems: The scale trend uses only three rungs; L4 and L6 have one seed per setting. The L4 and L6 fitted optima are at or beyond sweep edges, and only L3 receives a full two-dimensional tuning sweep. One planned larger rung was not run; one data mixture and tokenizer were used. The study reports held-out BPB, not training error or a train-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reportable result rows omitted. Cited prior-work findings were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD or momentum SGD performance under limited and broader tuning, including the specified recovery conditions.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout effects, including small-data, excessive-dropout and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps relative to other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Held-out BPB is a valid held-out performance measure; the reason V4 is untested is the missing adaptive-versus-SGD comparison, not the absence of a train-test gap. Changing depth, width, data volume and other architecture settings across rungs also does not test V2's post-interpolation width claim.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Generalization as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD, and tuning or recovery conditions for those methods.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures tracking the train-test gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.
